Global War 1936 v4.3 Rulebook · PDF p. 79 ↗

Chapter 12 - Place Units Phase#

Global War 1936 v4.3 Rulebook · PDF p. 79 ↗

12.1Place Units and Facilities#

Place units and facilities from the build queue place units box. Place facilities where they were started (i.e. where there is an Under Construction marker). If you cannot place a unit or facility due to a DoW during your Player Turn that affects your Supply Path, it remains in the place units box until the next Player Turn. When placing units and facilities the following apply:

• Land units or aircraft must be placed at a factory in a Supply Path with available capacity (refer to 13.2.1) which you have possessed since the beginning of the Player Turn. (May be interdicted, refer to 12.5).

• Naval units must be placed at a shipyard in a Supply Path with available capacity which you have possessed since the beginning of the Player Turn. Capital Ships must be placed at a Major Shipyard in a Supply Path with available capacity which you have possessed since the beginning of the Player Turn.

• Facilities must be placed in a land zone which you have possessed since the beginning of the Player Turn.

• A newly upgraded factory is not able to utilize its increased capacity until the next Player Turn.

• Surface Ships built at Major Shipyards may be placed in port (refer to 11.5).

• Militia are not built via factories. The number of Militia you may place in a land zone is equal to the land zone's IPP value with a minimum of one (even if the land zone has no IPP value). This limitation does not apply to recruitment rolls (refer to 12.7). You may place a maximum of 1 per Player Turn in non-Originally owned land zones. You must have possessed the land zone since the beginning of the Player Turn. Note that outside Home Country, the maximum number of Militia a Major Power can have in a land zone is equal to the IPP value of the zone, minimum of one. In Home Country there is no limit.

• Colonial Infantry are not built via factories. Colonial Infantry must be placed in land zones with a IPP value outside of Home Country. The maximum number which may be built per Player Turn in a land zone is equal to the land zone’s IPP value. The land zone must be Originally possessed. You must have possessed the land zone since the beginning of the Player Turn. Note that Colonial Infantry, like other specialty infantry, is limited to a maximum of two purchased per Player Turn.

CCP and KMT have a “Decentralized Production” special ability, refer to their reference sheets.

Example: A Major Factory has 3 damage. The owner paid for a full repair in the Production Phase. In the Place Unit Phase the owner is only able to place 2 units at this factory.

Example: Japan has a production capacity of 9. In the Production Phase, Japan buys 9 Infantry. During the Combat Movement Phase, Japan declares war on British Commonwealth, who has a Submarine in sea zone P14. In the Place Units Phase, Japan must attempt to place 1 Infantry in Rehe and risk interdiction.

Global War 1936 v4.3 Rulebook · PDF p. 79 ↗

12.2Repair#

Remove damage markers from repaired cities and facilities.

Damaged Capital Ships that have been at a Friendly dockyard or shipyard since the beginning of the Player Turn are now repaired (up to the available repair capacity (refer to 13.2.4 and 13.2.5)).

Ships that have been in port with skeleton crew since the beginning of the Player Turn are now reinforced.

Global War 1936 v4.3 Rulebook · PDF p. 80 ↗

12.3Upgrades#

Upgrading requires a Supply Path to the land zone that the unit or facility receiving the upgrade is in. A unit that has moved/attacked can be upgraded in the same Player Turn. If the upgrade cannot reach a suitable unit (due to casualties or units moving outside a Supply Path), the upgrade remains on the build queue until a Supply Path exists to a suitable unit in a future Place Units Phase.

A unit cannot be upgraded the same Player Turn it is placed on the board.

Global War 1936 v4.3 Rulebook · PDF p. 80 ↗

12.4Lend-lease Delivery#

You must start the Lend-lease delivery in your Home Country. The Lend-lease must then move along a Supply Path (refer to 1.11) to a land zone in the receiving nation’s Home Country. In other instances when tracing a Supply Path, you are only allowed to trace via naval facilities possessed by you or a Controlled/Aligned nation. However, when delivering Lend-lease, the naval facility at the final destination will be possessed by the receiving nation. All other naval facilities used to trace the Supply Path must be possessed, Controlled, or Aligned. All naval facilities used must be undamaged and possessed since the beginning of the Player Turn. Lend-lease units have no combat value during delivery. While traveling to its destination, the lend-leased unit is possessed by the sending nation. The Lend-lease stops in the first land zone in the receiving player’s possessed Home Country. Upon arrival at its destination, lend- leased sculpts may be replaced by the corresponding receiving nation’s sculpts. Lend-leased bases and Militia upgrades are moved to the recipients place units box on the build queue to be placed anywhere in their Home Country in their next Place Units Phase. Naval units can be delivered in port. Naval units cannot be delivered via land.

Interdiction: If the route passes through a sea zone with interdicting units, the Lend-lease may possibly be eliminated (refer to 12.5).

Blockade: A blockaded Naval Facility cannot send nor receive Lend-lease (refer to 9.4.6).

Failure to Deliver: Lend-lease that cannot be delivered must wait on the build queue and be attempted again on the next Player Turn.

12.5Interdiction#

Supply Paths can be interdicted if they pass through a sea zone that contains either:

• A non-Submerged submarine

• A Battlecruiser designated as a raider

• An aircraft on MAP

They can also be interdicted if they cross a narrow crossing with an Enemy Coastal Artillery.

Enemy units interdict; neutral eligible units may elect to interdict. A nation may not interdict a lend-lease delivery in route to itself.

Diplomatic relations for the interdicting nation:

At Peace With Sending NationAt War With Sending Nation
PrerequisitesAt Full Production or currently engaged in a civil war with the receiving nation.None
If SuccessfulSending nation gets a 1D6 income increase (cannot exceed Full Production).None
Table transcription · Check original layout ↗

For each sea zone where the delivery is interdicted, it is subject to interdiction die rolls. There are no die modifiers. If it scores a hit the delivery is eliminated.

The unit/facility attempting interdiction rolls a D12 using its attack values. If the interdicting player has developed Advanced Submarines technology, interdicting submarines double their attack values (i.e. a regular Submarine would hit on a “6” or less). After the attacker’s interdiction roll, ships designated as escorts get one defensive roll against each interdicting submarine and aircraft on MAP.

Example: Germany and Great Britain are at war. There is a German non-Submerged Submarine in the Supply Path for Great Britain’s Minor Factory in Cape Town. If the British player decides to place units in that facility, and the delivery is interdicted, the unit the British player wanted to place at the Minor Factory is eliminated.

Example: The Spanish Republicans want to interdict German Lend-lease to the Spanish Nationalists arriving in Galicia and León. They move their Coastal Submarine to sea zone A28 and in the next turn successfully interdict German Lend-lease. As Germany’s income level is already at Full Production, Germany does not get an income increase.

Example: Great Britain has developed Improved Factories technology and wishes to produce two units in its Minor Factory in Cape Town. An Enemy submarine successfully interdicts the Supply Path eliminating both units.

Global War 1936 v4.3 Rulebook · PDF p. 81 ↗

12.6Ships Captured in Port#

If conquering a land zone containing a Naval Facility with ships in port, roll a D12 for each ship:

Dice #Event
1-9Scuttled; Remove from game.
10-12Captured by Attacking player.
Table transcription · Check original layout ↗

The ship is captured in its current state regarding damage and/or skeleton crew.

Global War 1936 v4.3 Rulebook · PDF p. 82 ↗

12.7Recruitment Rolls#

Controlled Minor Powers (e.g. Abyssinia, Dadao Government, Mongolia, Nationalist Spain, Republican Spain, Siam and Vichy) make recruitment rolls. A recruitment roll is a D12. On a result that is equal to or less than the number of land zones that controlled nation Possesses*, you get either:

• 1 Infantry** or 2 Militia to place in land zones possessed by that controlled nation since the beginning of the Player Turn or

• Advancement of 1 ship on the controlled nation’s build queue or

• 1 full facility repair

* Offshore land zones do not count towards the number of land zones, except for Corsica (Vichy) and factions during an ongoing Spanish Civil War.

** Vichy gets 1 Foreign Legion to place in a land zone with a IPP value it has possessed since the beginning of the Player Turn.

Global War 1936 v4.3 Rulebook · PDF p. 82 ↗

12.8Influence Rolls#

Eligible nations roll for influence (refer to 15.2 and 15.4).

Global War 1936 v4.3 Rulebook · PDF p. 82 ↗

12.9Collect Income#

The Attacking player collects income. Note that some nations (British Commonwealth, France, USA, and USSR) start with a lower income that can gradually increase via income increases (refer to 5.2). The Axis nations begin at Full Production income and do not have income increases. Once a nation is at war with a Major Power, it also begins collecting Wartime Bonus Income (refer to 5.3). Controlled Minor Powers do not get IPP income (Exception: Vichy, refer to 4.11.3).

Global War 1936 v4.3 Rulebook · PDF p. 82 ↗

12.10End of Player Turn#

Remove IPP loss trackers on the Attacking Player's convoy lines.

Global War 1936 v4.3 Rulebook · PDF p. 82 ↗

12.11End of Round#

Once the USA player has collected income, it is the end of the round. If the Molotov- Ribbentrop Pact is in effect, Germany receives 5 IPP and USSR receives 3 IPP and 1 technology roll, simultaneously (refer to 6.4). Beginning July, 1944, the game end die roll is made (refer to 3.4). If the game continues, move the calendar marker on the top of the IPP tracking chart to the next turn.

13.1.1Infantry-class Units#

An infantry-class unit may pair with an artillery-class unit on a 1:1 ratio to give the paired infantry-class unit a +1 attack bonus. When defending in an unsurrounded city, infantry-class units get +1 defense bonus on all rounds of combat and Target Selection at “1” versus vehicle-class units. Fortifications add +2 defense bonus to all infantry-class units on the first round of combat (refer to 13.2.6). Infantry-class units may participate in the first round of an amphibious assault (refer to 10.8.3). Infantry-class units may non-combat move across narrow crossings (with some restrictions, refer to 1.9).

13.1.3Artillery-class Units#

Artillery-class units have the first strike ability on the first round of combat (refer to 10.2). An artillery-class unit may pair with an infantry-class unit on a 1:1 ratio to give the paired infantry- class unit a +1 attack bonus. Artillery-class units do not suffer the -1 attack penalty on the first round of combat for an attack across a river (refer to 1.7.6). Artillery-class units are minus -1 in attack/defense if not paired 1:1 with infantry-class or vehicle-class units.

Example: An army consisting of 10 artillery-class and 6 infantry-class units are attacked. 4 of the 10 artillery-class units defend at -1. In the first combat round, 3 of the defending infantry- class units are taken as casualties. In the second combat round, 7 of the 10 artillery-class units now defend at -1.

Existing register · outside pilot dates

Advanced Artillery city bombardment conditions

Project ruling: city bombardment uses attrition’s starting-adjacency and no-movement conditions. The gun remains in its original zone and fires at a city adjacent since the Player Turn began. City bombardment still deals 1D6 strategic damage; it does not use attrition’s hit-at-2 attack against units.

2026-10-22 · User-adopted interpretationRule register ↗

Ordinary attrition’s own restrictions are already explicit. This note concerns their extension to city bombardment only.

Naval units may be designated as being in port, which enables scrambling (refer to 11.5). Surface Warships may be designated as escorts (refer to 9.4.5). Three or more Surface Warships in a sea zone without Enemy units automatically blockade all Enemy Supply Paths in that sea zone, and all Naval Facilities adjacent to that sea zone (refer to 9.4.6).

Surface ships (excluding Battlecruisers designated as a raider) without Naval Supply have -1 movement.

13.2Facilities#

Cities can only contain one minor and one major Naval Facility. Facilities may grant a +1 movement bonus depending on where units start their movement:

• Aircraft other than seaplanes: in the same land zone as the Airbase.

• Seaplanes: in the same land zone as the Seaplane Base and only if the first sea zone entered is adjacent to this base.

• Submarines: in a sea zone adjacent to a Submarine Base in a Supply Path.

• Surface Ships: in a sea zone adjacent to a major Naval Facility in a Supply Path.

Global War 1936 v4.3 Rulebook · PDF p. 92–93 ↗

13.2.1Factories#

Factories represent the industrial production capacity of a land zone. There are three types of factories: Minor Factories, Medium Factories and Major Factories. All have inherent Anti-aircraft Artillery that defend against strategic bombing. The inherent Anti-aircraft Artillery of factories are never eliminated or taken as casualties. Factories do not have inherent Anti-aircraft Artillery while being constructed.

A Minor Factory outside Home Country needs a Supply Path. If this Supply Path is absent, blockaded or interdicted, the Minor Factory cannot produce any units.

A zone can contain more than one factory. The Player Turn a factory is built/captured it cannot produce anything. The Player Turn a factory is upgraded or repaired its production is limited to the production capacity it had at the start of the Player Turn. If captured, Medium and Major Factories are downgraded to a Minor Factory. The factory is captured in its current state regarding damage and in this particular situation, the maximum damage the factory may sustain is dependent on the factory’s original level. If repossessed by the original owner, the factory reverts to its original level in its current state of damage.

13.2.2Bases#

There are three types of bases: Airbases, Seaplane Bases, and Submarine Bases. These have some common features:

• Use: You can use it if you have possessed it since the beginning of your Player Turn or if you are Aligned to the nation that Possesses it.

• Anti-aircraft: All have inherent Anti-aircraft Artillery that defend against strategic bombing. The inherent Anti-aircraft Artillery of bases are never eliminated or taken as casualties. They do not have inherent Anti-aircraft Artillery while being constructed.

• Movement Bonus: A Supply Path is required. Having multiple bases of the same type does not provide a cumulative movement bonus.

13.2.6Fortifications#

A Fortification represents major defensive works established to prevent invasion. Fortifications are placed on a border of a land zone and protect from attacks across that border by Enemy units including border clashes (refer to 10.5.2), amphibious assaults (refer to 10.8), as well as airborne assaults (refer to 10.6.1).

Fortifications
Price5/5
WhereBorder of any possessed land zone. Only 1 Fortification per border may be built. The limit of 1 per per border also includes Fortifications from completing strategic objectives.
Table transcription · Check original layout ↗

Fortifications defend on the first round of combat at “5” with two first strike rolls except in airborne assaults where the Attacker has developed Airborne Doctrine technology. They add +2 defense bonus to all infantry-class units in the zone on the first round of combat.

Fortifications reduce these die rolls by 1:

• Shore bombardment

• Attrition attacks

• Carpet bombing in cities

Example: A Battleship that normally scores a shore bombardment hit on 1-4, is reduced to scoring a hit on 1-3.

Fortifications are removed if the zone is captured. Fortifications may neither be strategically bombed nor selected as a casualty.

Land units cannot blitz into a land zone border that contains an Enemy Fortification.

If attacking a land zone across multiple borders, with one of them having a Fortification, hits attributable to the Fortification must be taken from units that are attacking across its border. Such hits would include the two fortification first strikes and any hits specifically due to modification to rolls caused by the Fortification.

Example: USSR attacks Central Romania from Bulgaria and Bessarabia. Germany has a Fortification on the Central Romanian border towards Bessarabia. The German player gets one hit on the Fortification’s two first strike rolls. German Mountain Infantry also get a hit on a “6” in the first combat round. Both of these hits must be taken from attacking Soviet units coming from Bessarabia. Had the Mountain Infantry got a hit on a “5” instead, the Soviet player could freely choose a casualty.

France has a special Fortification - the “Maginot Line” - in Alsace-Lorraine on the border towards Bavaria. It protects from attacks by Enemy land units across that border. It defends on the first round of combat at “6” with two first strike rolls. It adds +3 defense bonus to all infantry-class units in the zone on the first round of combat. All attacking land units suffer double casualties on all combat rounds.

Global War 1936 v4.3 Rulebook · PDF p. 97–98 ↗

13.2.7Coastal Artillery#

Coastal Artillery represents artillery emplacements along a land/sea zone border to defend against amphibious assaults.

Coastal Artillery
Price6
WhereAny possessed land zone bordering one or more sea zones. Multiple Coastal Artillery may be built on the same border.
Table transcription · Check original layout ↗

Each Coastal Artillery gets one first strike defense roll at “3” per attacking ship shore bombarding and/or unloading units in the amphibious assault up to a maximum of three shots. The amphibiously assaulting player chooses casualties.

Coastal Artillery located at narrow crossings may fire at each Enemy Surface Ship at “3” that passes through the narrow crossing (up to a maximum of three shots per Player Turn). This also includes when scrambling out of a Naval Facility (refer to 10.4) or going in port (refer to 11.5).

Example: Great Britain scrambles a Destroyer out of the Major Shipyard in London into sea zone A23. Germany Possesses a Coastal Artillery in Picardy. As the British Destroyer crosses the narrow crossing line, the Coastal Artillery gets to fire.

Coastal Artillery only ever get to fire up to three shots per Player Turn.

Example: Japan and the Commonwealth are at war. Japan moves a Heavy Cruiser and two Naval Transports from I12 to P50 and then amphibiously assaults British Malaya. The British Coastal Artillery only gets to fire three shots.

Coastal artillery is removed if the zone is captured. They may neither be strategically bombed nor selected as a casualty.

Global War 1936 v4.3 Rulebook · PDF p. 98–99 ↗

13.2.8Railroads#

Railroads are placed on land zone borders. If a land zone has a border with a crossing railroad, the entire zone is considered to be “covered” with rail.

• Use: You can use it if you have possessed it since the beginning of your Player Turn or if you are Aligned to the nation that Possesses it.

• Anti-aircraft: Railroads do not have inherent Anti-aircraft Artillery.

Railroads can be strategically bombed (refer to 10.6.2). If USSR is using its “Scorched Earth” special ability to destroy railroads, this is being done on borders between land zones.

Normal TerrainDesert/Jungle/Marsh/Mountain/Tundra

Use if DamagedUseless if damaged

Cost to Repair1 IPP per damage point

Determine the terrain by tracing the most direct line from the originating land zone roundel to the target land zone roundel. The terrain on the border determines the type of terrain, and thus the price.

Example: the border of Sudan and Belgian Congo is normal and jungle terrain, so the cost is 4 IPP.

A new railroad is placed on one land zone border, and connects these two land zones via rail.

14.1Spanish Civil War#

Spanish Civil War
ForcesSpanish Nationalists controlled by Germany versus Spanish Republicans controlled by USSR.
ParticipationSpanish factions are controlled Minor Powers. They can only move/ attack within Spain and in sea zones adjacent to Spanish Nationalist or Spanish Republican Originally possessed land zones. As long as the civil war is on-going, no foreign nations may intervene/attack Spanish units or land zones. Eligible nations may send Lend-lease.
Axis SupportGermany and Italy may both send Lend-lease to the Nationalists. Germany may create the Condor Legion (refer to 15.1).
Comintern SupportUSSR may send Lend-lease to the Republicans.
Allies’ SupportThe Allies may send Militia upgrades as Lend-lease to both factions. Only one Allies’ Major Power may send Lend-lease per Calendar Turn.
IncomeRepublicans and Nationalists neither collect nor spend income, but make recruitment rolls (refer to 12.7). Note that both factions use all land zones for recruitment roll purposes.
Victory & ResolutionEnds when one faction Possesses all 6 continental Spanish land zones. Upon resolution of the Spanish Civil War, the vanquished faction ceases to exist and the victor becomes neutral (refer to 4.10).
AftermathRemove any remaining units from the defeated faction and repair any damage to Spanish facilities.

ParticipationCCP and KMT fight using normal rules. Other nations may not enter any Originally possessed KMT, CCP, or warlord land zones without a DoW, even if that land zone is Friendly. (Exception: Dadao Government, refer to 15.4). Eligible nations may send Lend-lease (refer to 8.7, 15.3 and 15.4).
TruceWhen a foreign Major Power declares war on China, CCP and KMT may agree to a truce (refer to 6.6).
DurationEnds when one faction no longer has any surviving units.

Global War 1936 v4.3 Rulebook · PDF p. 101 ↗

14.3.1Evolution to Major Power#

Until evolved, CCP and KMT do not Align with anyone. They can only move/attack within Chinese Home Country and in sea zones adjacent to Chinese Home Country.

Evolution to Major Power: CCP and KMT evolve to a Major Power if their land zone IPP values add to 13+ IPP. After evolving, they select a Capital and may place 1 factory there at no cost:

• 1 Major Factory if chosen Capital is a city land zone.

• 1 Medium Factory if chosen Capital is any other land zone.

Subsequently, they can build facilities, send Lend-lease, develop technology and move/attack outside Chinese Home Country.

As a Major Power, CCP neither gets recruitments nor influence rolls. In addition, it no longer has the “Decentralized Production” special ability (refer to 15.2). As a Major Power, KMT no longer has “Decentralized Production” or “Low Morale” special abilities (refer to 15.7).

Note that if CCP or KMT evolve to a Major Power in their respective Player Turns, they can still use their “Decentralized Production” special ability in that turn.

Global War 1936 v4.3 Rulebook · PDF p. 102 ↗

Chapter 15 - National Special Abilities#

Each nation has some special abilities unique to that nation. Special abilities supersede normal rules when in conflict (i.e. “Decentralized Production”).

Global War 1936 v4.3 Rulebook · PDF p. 102–103 ↗

15.1Germany#

Special Abilities
Condor LegionGermany has +1 Supply Path range when delivering Lend-lease to the Spanish Nationalists as well as when transferring the Condor Legion to and from Spain. Once per game, while the Spanish Civil War is ongoing, the Condor Legion can be created in the Production Phase by moving a German Fighter in a Supply Path already on the board to the place units box. Cost to implement: 5 IPP. During the Place Units Phase, the Condor Legion is transferred to a Spanish Nationalist-possessed land zone via a Supply Path. This transfer does not require strategic rail or Strategic Naval Movement. Subject to interdiction (refer to 12.5). The Spanish Republicans get an extra recruitment roll on the next Spanish Republican Player Turn the Condor Legion is created. While in Spain, the Condor Legion is a Spanish Nationalist unit. The Condor Legion can be recalled back to German Home Country at no cost during the Non-combat Movement Phase if the Spanish Nationalists win the Spanish Civil War. Requires a Supply Path. Subject to interdiction (refer to 12.5).
BlitzkriegOnce per game, and prior to July, 1941, all German land and air units may make an additional sequence of combat movement, combat (including blitz) and non-combat movement. The second sequence of attacks takes place immediately after the end of the first non-combat movement. All participating land and air units have their movement allowance reset after the first sequence. In the second sequence, land units may not combat move or non-combat move through just captured land zones. Units with blitz may use this ability both sequences if possible. Attacking vehicle-class units do not suffer -2 attack penalty when attacking cities. On the turn Blitzkrieg is used, Strategic Rail Movement only occurs during the second sequence of non-combat movement. Example: Germany attacks Belgium and blitzes into Picardy in the first sequence. In the second sequence, the German player wants to attack Paris. Units in Belgium with a movement of “2” are not able to participate.
Technological SuperiorityCan purchase Medium Armor, Mechanized Infantry, Strategic Bombers and Tank Destroyers earlier than other nations, beginning July, 1938.
Table transcription · Check original layout ↗
Special Abilities
Operation BarbarossaOnce per game, if Germany declares war on USSR, in the subsequent German Combat Phase, all German land and air units get +1 attack against Soviet units and all Soviet units get -1 defense on all rounds of combat and subsequent blitzes. USSR may not attack more than one German-possessed land zone on its next Player Turn following this combat phase. (Note: Germany can not use this special ability if USSR declares war first).
Deutsches Afrika Korps (DAK)Prerequisite: Italy is at war with an Allies’ Major Power. Once per game, DAK can be created in the Production Phase by moving German units in a Supply Path and already on the board to the place units box. DAK may consist of up to 3 Infantry, up to 1 Motorized Infantry, up to 2 artillery-class units and up to 2 Light Armor (or 1 Light and 1 Medium). Cost to implement: 1 IPP per unit, maximum of 5 IPP regardless of the number of DAK units created. At the end of the Place Units Phase, DAK units are transferred to a Friendly Originally Italian-possessed North African land zone via a Supply Path. This transfer does not require strategic rail or Strategic Naval Movement. Normal Supply Path rules apply (refer to 1.11). Note each DAK unit is a separate delivery. DAK units are unaffected by desert terrain rules. If a DAK unit is eliminated, the German player may in subsequent Production Phases send a replacement of the same type. Cost per unit: 1 IPP. Same transfer rules apply. DAK units can be recalled back to German Home Country at no cost during the Non-combat Movement Phase. Requires a Supply Path. Subject to interdiction (refer to 12.5).

Decentralized ProductionCCP may place infantry-class units and Cavalry in any Chinese Home Country land zone it has possessed since the beginning of the Player Turn. No factory is required.
RecruitmentDuring the Place Units Phase, CCP may make one recruitment roll. If the roll is less than or equal to the total number of land zones CCP Possesses, CCP may place one Infantry or two Militia in any of those land zones (according to the rules for “Decentralized Production,” above).
Comintern BrothersIf there is an undamaged railroad connecting a CCP-possessed land zone to a Soviet-possessed land zone in the Production Phase, it may purchase Artillery and Anti-aircraft Artillery units. These must be placed in the land zone with this railroad.

Spreading InfluenceDuring the Place Units Phase, CCP may make one influence roll on a Chinese warlord adjacent to an Influencing Zone. 15.3USSR#

Special Abilities
InefficiencyAligned/captured land zones do not increase Soviet income until USSR reaches its Full Production income via income increase rolls or from an Enemy declaring war on USSR. Note that income from Annexed land zones can be collected immediately.
Factory MovementOnce at war with a Major Power, USSR may use 1 Strategic Rail Move to move a Minor or Medium Factory and 2 Strategic Rail Moves to move a Major Factory within Soviet Home Country. The factory cannot produce any units or technology, or be upgraded or repaired the Player Turn it moves. It moves in whatever state of damage it has suffered. If USSR has achieved its “Access to the Mediterranean” strategic objective, it can move one Minor Factory each Player Turn without the Home Country restriction and ignoring Railroad gauge changes.
Northern Sea RouteUSSR can move one naval unit per Player Turn between sea zones A9 and P1 (in either direction). The unit must start its move in either sea zone A9 or P1, and it expends its full movement (including any bonuses) to make the move. USSR may give other nations permission to use this route.
For the Motherland!In the first Production Phase that USSR is at war with a Major Power all units cost -1 IPP. USSR may use its Militia for attacking in its Home Country paired 1:1 with other land units.
Scorched EarthUSSR can destroy its own facilities during the Combat Phase of its Player Turn. Land zone must have been in the Soviet player’s Possession since the beginning of the Player Turn. No land unit is required. Destroyed facilities cannot be repaired.

International Red AidCCP: During the Place Units Phase, one Soviet air transport in a Supply Path which has not moved or been placed this turn may Lend-lease deliver a Militia upgrade to CCP. The air transport uses its range to travel to the recipient-possessed land zone, may fly over Warlord-possessed land zones, and must land in a Soviet-possessed land zone after delivery. Spanish Republicans: If Turkey is a Non-controlled neutral nation, USSR may trace a Supply Path to deliver Lend-lease to the Spanish Republicans through the Turkish Straits even if USSR is at war with a Major Power.

15.4Japan#

Special Abilities
Dadao GovernmentDuring the Place Units Phase, Japan may make one influence roll on a Chinese warlord adjacent to an Influencing Zone. If the roll is less than or equal to the total number of adjacent land zones Japan Controls/Possesses, all remaining land zones and military units of that warlord Align and become/join a Japanese-controlled Axis Minor Power: Dadao Government. Note that impassable borders do not count for adjacency. Prior to rolling, Japan may spend IPP up to the amount of its original influence roll to increase the chance of success. Each IPP spent subtracts 1 from the influence roll. Regardless of how much is spent, the Influence attempt backfires on a “12” causing the warlord to Align with KMT instead. As long as controlled, the Dadao Government gets recruitment rolls, and may receive Lend-lease from Japan. It may attack Chinese land zones without the rest of China Aligning with CCP or KMT. If attacked by CCP or KMT, it does not Align with Japan. If Japan is at war with both China and a Major Power, Dadao Aligns with Japan.
KamikazeWhen USA reaches Wartime Income, Japan may make up to 2 kamikaze attacks per Calendar Turn to a game total of 6. These are made at an attack of 7 vs. Surface Ships with first strike and Target Selection of “1-3”. No aircraft is required or expended for these attacks. Kamikaze attacks may be made from Japanese Home Country and have a range of 4 sea zones. These sea zones are depicted with a small “Kamikaze” symbol on the map. Kamikazes may not be used in port attacks. Kamikazes may also be used when Japan is the Defender in a sea zone adjacent to Japanese Home Country or during the shore bombardment phase of an amphibious assault on Japanese Home Country.

Special Abilities
Surprise AttackJapan may, as a DoW, make one surprise attack on one land or sea zone (or one sea zone subsequently followed by an amphibious assault on an adjacent land zone, with “Surprise Attack” for both) the first time it declares war on an Allies’ Major Power. In this zone, all Japanese aircraft gain first strike. All Enemy units receive a -1 defense on the first round of combat. Scrambling is not allowed into combat subject to a surprise attack (refer to 10.4). If the surprise attack is used on a port attack (refer to 10.6.4), the inherent facility Anti-aircraft Artillery does not get to defend. If the surprise attack is used to attack a city land zone, combat is not limited to three rounds of combat. Japanese ships and aircraft on Carriers gain +1 combat movement bonus to reach this zone. This movement bonus is cumulative with other movement bonuses. Example: A ship with a movement of 3 adjacent to a Major Port, will have a total movement of 5.
Destroyer TransportsMay transport Marines on its Destroyers, one per ship. These may amphibiously assault from the Destroyer. While transporting Marines, Destroyers have -1 movement. May not continue moving after unloading.
Dug in DefenseJapanese infantry-class units defending in their Home Country gain +1 defense bonus.

15.7KMT#

Special Abilities
Decentralized ProductionKMT may place infantry-class units and Cavalry in any Chinese Home Country land zone it has possessed since the beginning of the Player Turn. No factory is required.
Low MoraleUpon attacking, each KMT regular Infantry and Cavalry that rolls a 10 or more retreats from the attack to the zone it attacked from. These units must roll dice, even if there are no defending units in the land zone they are attacking. Units that are forced to retreat may not be taken as casualties. If KMT has evolved to a Major Power, it no longer suffers this attack weakness.
Burma and Ledo RoadsAllows tracing a Supply Path through the otherwise impassable Himalayan Mountains for Lend-lease delivery. It cannot be strategically bombed. It requires the following four conditions in order to be open: 1. It must be July, 1938 or later. 2. Japan and KMT are at war. 3. KMT Possesses Yunnan. 4. The Allies Possess Burma. While the Burma Road is open, KMT may purchase Artillery and Anti-aircraft Artillery in Yunnan. The Ledo Road extends the Burma Road to Bengal. Same conditions and rules apply, but the Allies must also Possess Bengal.

Special Abilities
Monroe DoctrineThe “Monroe Doctrine” allows USA to attack Comintern units that are bordering North or South American land zones regardless of its own income level without declaring war. USA is also allowed to attack Comintern-occupied land zones in North and South America. Comintern violations of the “Monroe Doctrine” do not trigger USA income increases. If an Axis Major Power attacks a land zone in North or South America, or has a Surface Ship ends its movement within 3 sea zones of USA Home Country, USA considers it a declaration of war. Sea zones affected by this are depicted by a small “Monroe” symbol on the map.
Operation OverlordOnce per game, in January, 1943 or later, USA units and British Commonwealth units may together amphibiously attack a German-possessed land zone bordering an Atlantic Ocean (A##) sea zone during the USA player’s turn. Both nations may use one another’s naval and air transports. Aircraft and airborne assaulting units may participate in the attack. Eligible warships may provide shore bombardment. The participating British Commonwealth units may not have moved or been placed during the British Commonwealth player's turn. USA takes possession of the captured land zone.

Chapter 16 - Designer Notes#

Realism vs. Playability: Global War is meant to be a fun, balanced game that takes players back to the years before the Second World War. As such, you will notice many elements of history that have been changed to be ahistorical for the sake of improving playability.

Balance: Balance is paramount for a game like Global War. We have put a lot of emphasis into fine- tuning the balance of each component, striving to holistically improving the game overall.

Time is an important element. Early-to-mid game, the Axis should be overwhelmingly strong. Mid-to-late game the balance will start to shift towards an Allies’ victory. Comintern, as the 3rd alliance, is the joker in the mix. They have equal possibility to win as the other two alliances. The new variable ending die roll ensures excitement to the very last minute and eliminates late-game player gimmicks to earn victory points.

Longevity: The changes that were made in version 4 help ensure Global War will continue to be fun to play for many years to come. Testing has shown that players continue to evolve their strategies even after playing dozens of games. As soon as a “winning strategy” emerges, players will quickly be able to adapt with counter strategies.

Building a close-knit gaming group of dedicated people is the dream of many players. Historical Board Gaming hopes that the many improvements that were made for version 4 will grow the community of players and enable more people to realize this dream in the future.

                        Evolution to Major Power:

                        13+ IPP. After evolving, it selects a Capital and may place 1 factory
                        there at no cost:

                        • 1 Major Factory if chosen capital is a city land zone.
                        • 1 Medium Factory if chosen capital is any other land zone.
                        Subsequently, it can build facilities, send Lend-lease, develop
                        technology and move/attack outside Chinese Home Country.

                        As a Major Power, CCP neither gets recruitments nor influence rolls. In
                        addition, it no longer has the “Decentralized Production” special ability.
                        Note that if CCP evolves to a Major Power in its Player Turn, it can still
                        use its “Decentralized Production” special ability in that turn.
 Surrender              CCP never surrenders.

 Special Abilities


                            Special Ability
 Decentralized              CCP may place infantry-class units and Cavalry in any Chinese Home
 Production                 Country land zone it has possessed since the beginning of the Player
                            Turn. No factory is required.

 Recruitment                During the Place Units Phase, CCP may make one recruitment roll. If
                            the roll is less than or equal to the total number of land zones CCP
                            Possesses, CCP may place one Infantry or two Militia in any of those
                            land zones (according to the rules for “Decentralized Production”,
                            above).

 Spreading Influence        During the Place Units Phase, CCP may make one influence roll on a
                            Chinese warlord adjacent to an Influencing Zone. If the roll is less than
                            or equal to the total number of adjacent land zones CCP Possesses, all
                            remaining land zones and military units of that warlord Align with CCP.
                            Prior to rolling, CCP may spend IPP up to the amount of its original
                            influence roll to increase the chance of success. Each IPP spent
                            subtracts 1 from the influence roll. Regardless of how much is spent,
                            the Influence attempt backfires on a “12” causing the warlord to Align
                            with KMT instead.

 Comintern Brothers         If there is an undamaged railroad connecting a CCP-possessed land
                            zone to a Soviet-possessed land zone in the Production Phase, it may
                            purchase Artillery and Anti-aircraft Artillery units. These must be placed
                            in the land zone with this railroad.

◇Project choiceRCL-002
Existing register · outside pilot dates

Influence spending cap before rolling

Project ruling: use the unmodified success threshold as the pre-roll spending cap. Spend an integer no greater than that threshold and available treasury; subtract the spending from the die result. A natural 12 still backfires. The phrase “original influence roll” is not treated as a die that has already been rolled.

2026-10-05 · User-adopted interpretationRule register ↗

Not independently publisher-confirmed; this is a settled project choice for ambiguous spending wording.

✓Correction / fixRCL-004
Existing register · outside pilot dates

CCP purchases: railroad wording, not a generic supply path

Use the undamaged railroad connection from CCP-possessed land to Soviet-possessed land required by Comintern Brothers, including its placement restriction. A sea-only or river-only supply path does not unlock these Artillery/AAA purchases. The user reports that the developers fixed the inconsistent purchase-note wording for the next version.

2026-10-17 · Developer fix reported by userRule register ↗

Reported developer resolution; a subsequently published replacement sheet has not been verified here.

                                   Free France
 Overview


                 Does not have a Home Country.
 Home Country    As Free France does not have a Home Country, it cannot build Medium or Major
                 Factories, Major Dockyards, Major Shipyards or Capital Ships.

                 Starts at war with Vichy and all nations France was at war with before
 Diplomacy       surrendering.

                 After France surrenders, Free France must choose its capital in any of Free
 Capital         France’s remaining possessed land zones after the creation of Vichy. If captured,
                 Free France may move its Capital (refer to 10.10.3).
                 Collects income from French dominions it took possession of in the Vichy rolls
 Income
                 after the fall of France (and any captured land zones).
 Strategic Navel
                 0
 Moves
 Alignments      Free France Aligns with any Allies’ Major Power at war with the Axis.
                 Free France may receive Lend-lease in its Capital (refer to 12.4).
 Lend-lease
                 Free France may not send Lend-lease.
                 As Free France does not have a Home Country, it does not need to trace a
 Production
                 Supply Path to its Minor Factories (refer to 13.2.1).

 Technology      Free France is not able to research technology.
                 Immediately after Paris is liberated, France is resurrected and Free France
                 ceases to exist (refer to 4.11.1). All French land zones possessed by the Allies’
                 are returned to them.
 France
                 Immediately after the liberation of Paris, France receives 4 Militia representing
                 local resistance that may be placed in any French-possessed land zone in
                 French Home Country.
 Surrender       Free France never surrenders.

Special Abilities


                             Special Abilities
 Blitzkrieg                  Once per game, and prior to July, 1941, all German land and air units
                             may make an additional sequence of combat movement, combat
                             (including blitz) and non-combat movement. The second sequence of
                             attacks takes place immediately after the end of the first non-combat
                             movement. All participating land and air units have their movement
                             allowance reset after the first sequence. In the second sequence, land
                             units may not combat move or non-combat move through just
                             captured land zones. Units with blitz may use this ability both
                             sequences if possible. Attacking vehicle-class units do not suﬀer -2
                             attack penalty when attacking cities. On the turn Blitzkrieg is used,
                             Strategic Rail Movement only occurs during the second sequence of
                             non-combat movement.

                             Example: Germany attacks Belgium and blitzes into Picardy in the first
                             sequence. In the second sequence, the German player wants to attack
                             Paris. Units in Belgium with a movement of “2” are not able to
                             participate.

Source layout
                          Special Abilities
 Condor Legion            Germany has +1 Supply Path range when delivering Lend-lease to the
                          Spanish Nationalists as well as when transferring the Condor Legion to
                          and from Spain.

                          Once per game, while the Spanish Civil War is ongoing, the Condor
                          Legion can be created in the Production Phase by moving a German
                          Fighter in a Supply Path already on the board to the place units box.
                          Cost to implement: 5 IPP.

                          During the Place Units Phase, the Condor Legion is transferred to a
                          Spanish Nationalist-possessed land zone via a Supply Path. This
                          transfer does not require strategic rail or Strategic Naval
                          Movement. Subject to interdiction (refer to 12.5). The Spanish
                          Republicans get an extra recruitment roll on the next Spanish
                          Republican Player Turn the Condor Legion is created.

                          While in Spain, the Condor Legion is a Spanish Nationalist unit.

                          The Condor Legion can be recalled back to German Home Country at
                          no cost during the Non-combat Movement Phase if the Spanish
                          Nationalists win the Spanish Civil War. Requires a Supply Path. Subject
                          to interdiction (refer to 12.5).

 Operation Barbarossa Once per game, if Germany declares war on USSR, in the subsequent
                          German Combat Phase, all German land and air units get +1 attack
                          against Soviet units and all Soviet units get -1 defense on all rounds of
                          combat and subsequent blitzes. USSR may not attack more than one
                          German-possessed land zone on its next Player Turn following this
                          combat phase. (Note: Germany can not use this special ability if USSR
                          declares war first).
 Deutsches Afrika         Prerequisite: Italy is at war with an Allies’ Major Power.
 Korps (DAK)
                          Once per game, DAK can be created in the Production Phase by
                          moving German units in a Supply Path and already on the board to the
                          place units box. DAK may consist of up to 3 Infantry, up to 1 Motorized
                          Infantry, up to 2 artillery-class units and up to 2 Light Armor (or 1 Light
                          and 1 Medium). Cost to implement: 1 IPP per unit, maximum of 5 IPP
                          regardless of the number of DAK units created.

                          At the end of the Place Units Phase, DAK units are transferred to a
                          Friendly Originally Italian-possessed North African land zone via a
                          Supply Path. This transfer does not require strategic rail or Strategic
                          Naval Movement. Normal Supply Path rules apply (refer to 1.11). Note
                          each DAK unit is a separate delivery.

                          DAK units are unaﬀected by desert terrain rules.

                          If a DAK unit is eliminated, the German player may in subsequent
                          Production Phases send a replacement of the same type. Cost per
                          unit: 1 IPP. Same transfer rules apply.

                          DAK units can be recalled back to German Home Country at no cost
                          during the Non-combat Movement Phase. Requires a Supply Path.
                          Subject to interdiction (refer to 12.5).

Source layout
     Special Abilities

                             Special Abilities
       Dadao Government      During the Place Units Phase, Japan may make one influence roll on a
                             Chinese warlord adjacent to an Influencing Zone. If the roll is less than or
                             equal to the total number of adjacent land zones Japan Controls/
                             Possesses, all remaining land zones and military units of that warlord
                             Align and become/join a Japanese-controlled Axis Minor Power: Dadao
                             Government. Note that impassable borders do not count for adjacency.
                             Prior to rolling, Japan may spend IPP up to the amount of its original
                             influence roll to increase the chance of success. Each IPP spent
                             subtracts 1 from the influence roll. Regardless of how much is spent, the
                             Influence attempt backfires on a “12” causing the warlord to Align with
                             KMT instead.

                             As long as controlled, the Dadao Government gets recruitment rolls, and
                             may receive Lend-lease from Japan. It may attack Chinese land zones
                             without the rest of China Aligning with CCP or KMT.

                             If attacked by CCP or KMT, it does not Align with Japan. If Japan is at
                             war with both China and a Major Power, Dadao Aligns with Japan.
       Dug in Defense        Japanese infantry-class units defending in their Home Country gain +1
                             defense bonus.
       Kamikaze              When USA reaches Wartime Income, Japan may make up to 2 kamikaze
                             attacks per Calendar Turn to a game total of 6. These are made at an
                             attack of 7 vs. Surface Ships with first strike and Target Selection of
                             “1-3”. No aircraft is required or expended for these attacks. Kamikaze
                             attacks may be made from Japanese Home Country and have a range of
                             4 sea zones. These sea zones are depicted with a small “Kamikaze”
                             symbol on the map. Kamikazes may not be used in port attacks.

                             Kamikazes may also be used when Japan is the Defender in a sea zone
                             adjacent to Japanese Home Country or during the shore bombardment
                             phase of an amphibious assault on Japanese Home Country.
       Surprise Attack       Japan may, as a DoW, make one surprise attack on one land or sea zone
                             (or one sea zone subsequently followed by an amphibious assault on an
                             adjacent land zone, with “Surprise Attack” for both) the first time it
                             declares war on an Allies’ Major Power. In this zone, all Japanese aircraft
                             gain first strike. All Enemy units receive a -1 defense on the first round of
                             combat. Scrambling is not allowed into combat subject to a surprise
                             attack (refer to 10.4). If the surprise attack is used on a port attack (refer
                             to 10.6.4), the inherent facility Anti-aircraft Artillery does not get to
                             defend. If the surprise attack is used to attack a city land zone, combat
                             is not limited to three rounds of combat.
                             Japanese ships and aircraft on Carriers gain +1 combat movement
                             bonus to reach this zone. This movement bonus is cumulative with other
                             movement bonuses.
                             Example: A ship with a movement of 3 adjacent to a Major Port, will have
                             a total movement of 5.
       Destroyer             May transport Marines on its Destroyers, one per ship. These may
                             amphibiously assault from the Destroyer. While transporting Marines,
       Transports            Destroyers have -1 movement. May not continue moving after unloading.

Discussion attached to this rule
◇Project choiceRCL-002
Existing register · outside pilot dates

Influence spending cap before rolling

Project ruling: use the unmodified success threshold as the pre-roll spending cap. Spend an integer no greater than that threshold and available treasury; subtract the spending from the die result. A natural 12 still backfires. The phrase “original influence roll” is not treated as a die that has already been rolled.

2026-10-05 · User-adopted interpretationRule register ↗

Not independently publisher-confirmed; this is a settled project choice for ambiguous spending wording.

◇Project choiceRCL-010
Existing register · outside pilot dates

Dadao lend-lease destination

Project ruling pending developer clarification: Japanese lend-lease may be delivered to any Dadao-possessed land within Chinese Home Country, subject to all ordinary supply-route, timing, blockade and item limits. This supplies a destination for the explicit aid permission when Dadao has no original Home Country; it does not redefine Dadao’s Home Country for other rules.

2026-10-22 · User-adopted campaign interpretationRule register ↗

Genuine missing delivery destination; no developer ruling has been reported.

                              Evolution to Major Power:
                              KMT evolves to a Major Power once its land zone IPP values add up
                              to 13+ IPP. After evolving, it selects a Capital and may place 1 factory
                              there at no cost:

                              • 1 Major Factory if chosen capital is a city land zone.
                              • 1 Medium Factory if chosen capital is any other land zone.
                              Subsequently, it can build facilities, send Lend-lease, develop
                              technology and move/attack outside Chinese Home Country.

                              As a Major Power, KMT no longer has “Decentralized Production” or
                              “Low Morale” special abilities. Note that if KMT evolves to a Major
                              Power in its Player Turn, it can still use its “Decentralized Production”
                              special ability in that turn.
       Surrender              Surrenders if KMT Possesses no land zones.

Special Abilities

                              Special Ability
 I Want You!                  The first time USA is at war with a Major Power, infantry-class units
                              cost -1 IPP in the next USA Production Phase.

 Monroe Doctrine              The “Monroe Doctrine” allows USA to attack Comintern units that are
                              bordering North or South American land zones regardless of its own
                              income level without declaring war. USA is also allowed to attack Com-
                              intern-occupied land zones in North and South America. Comintern
                              violations of the “Monroe Doctrine” do not trigger USA peacetime in-
                              come increases.

                              If an Axis Major Power attacks a land zone in North or South America,
                              or has a Surface Ship ends its movement within 3 sea zones of USA
                              Home Country, USA considers it a declaration of war. Sea zones af-
                              fected by this are depicted by a small “Monroe” symbol on the map.
 Operation Overlord           Once per game, in January, 1943 or later, USA units and British Com-
                              monwealth units may together amphibiously attack a German-pos-
                              sessed land zone bordering an Atlantic Ocean (A##) sea zone during
                              the USA player’s turn. Aircraft and airborne assaulting units may partic-
                              ipate in the attack. Eligible warships may provide shore bombardment.
                              The participating British Commonwealth units may not have moved or
                              been placed during the British Commonwealth player's turn. USA takes
                              possession of the captured land zone.

 Contain Communism            USA may, at any income level, send Lend-lease to KMT, if CCP has
                              received Lend-lease from USSR during that Calendar Turn. (Exception:
                              When USSR uses its “International Red Aid” special ability.)

                              USA may use FEC-, French-, or Free French-possessed facilities to
                              deliver this Lend-lease.

     Special Abilities

                              Special Abilities
     Inefficiency             Aligned/captured land zones do not increase Soviet income until USSR
                              reaches its Full Production income via income increase rolls or from an
                              Enemy declaring war on USSR. Note that income from Annexed land
                              zones can be collected immediately.

     Factory Movement         Once at war with a Major Power, USSR may use 1 Strategic Rail Move
                              to move a Minor or Medium Factory and 2 Strategic Rail Moves to
                              move a Major Factory within Soviet Home Country. The factory cannot
                              produce any units or technology, or be upgraded or repaired the Player
                              Turn it moves. It moves in whatever state of damage it has su ered.

                              If USSR has achieved its “Access to the Mediterranean” strategic
                              objective, it can move one Minor Factory each Player Turn without the
                              Home Country restriction and ignoring Railroad gauge changes.

     Northern Sea Route       USSR can move one naval unit per Player Turn between sea zones A9
                              and P1 (in either direction). The unit must start its move in either sea
                              zone A9 or P1, and it expends its full movement (including any
                              bonuses) to make the move. USSR may give other nations permission
                              to use this route.

     For the Motherland!      In the rst Production Phase that USSR is at war with a Major Power
                              all units cost -1 IPP.

                              USSR may use its Militia for attacking in its Home Country paired 1:1
                              with other land units.
     Scorched Earth           USSR can destroy its own facilities during the Combat Phase of its
                              Turn. Land zone must have been in the Soviet player’s Possession
                              since the beginning of the Player Turn. No land unit is required.
                              Destroyed facilities cannot be repaired.

     International Red Aid    CCP:
                              During the Place Units Phase, one Soviet air transport in a Supply Path
                              which has not moved or been placed this turn may Lend-lease deliver
                              a Militia upgrade to CCP. The Air Transport uses its range to travel to
                              the recipient-possessed land zone, may y over Warlord-possessed
                              land zones, and must land in a Soviet-possessed land zone after
                              delivery.

                              Spanish Republicans:
                              If Turkey is a Non-controlled neutral nation, USSR may trace a Supply
                              Path to deliver Lend-lease to the Spanish Republicans through the
                              Turkish Straits even if USSR is at war with a Major Power.

                   Global War 1936
                                        v4.3

                       National Reference Sheet

                                      Vichy
Overview



 Home Country      Corsica and Southern France.
                   Axis Minor Power Controlled by Germany.
 Diplomacy         Starts at war with Free France. May not conduct diplomacy.
 Capital           Does not have a Capital. May collect income without a Capital.
                   Collects income from its Home Country and the French dominions it
                   took possession of in the Vichy rolls after the fall of France (and any
                   captured land zones).

 Income            When collecting income each turn, the German player decides how
                   income from Vichy-possessed land zones should be allocated.
                   Either:
                   • Added to the German income (to be spent as Germany) or
                   • Collected by Vichy (to be spent as Vichy)
 Strategic Navel
                   0
 Moves

                   Vichy may receive Lend-lease from Germany.
 Lend-lease
                   Vichy may not send Lend-lease.
                   Decentralized Production ability. May place facilities, Militia and
 Production &
                   Foreign Legion in land zones it has possessed since the beginning of
 Factories
                   the Player Turn. No factory is required.
 Technology        Vichy is not able to research technology.
                   If Paris is liberated, Vichy surrenders immediately. All remaining
 Surrender         Vichy units and land zones subsequently join France.
